description: We have decided to go duo only. We are not accepting anyone else. Apologies for any inconvenience.
summary:
The project is made with the monomanical aim of catering to the young and casual audience, and to instill scientific curiosity within them. 

Every human is born with innate curiosity and wonder. If it wasn't so, then our ancestors would have never left the valleys of Africa to explore the world. We are as curious about the unknown as we are afraid. 

Every child is wondrous about space, as we grow up, that curiosity gets suppressed under reticence and conformity. Our aim is to rekindle that curiosity with simple and "cool-looking" infographics that cradled most of our childhoods. 

This is done through anthropomorphizing the stories of our abandoned explorers. They are kept short and brief on purpose, which engages both the curious mind while also dabbling in the scientific propensity and temperament. 

Join us in sharing the Stories of our Fallen Explorers!
details:
Stories of the Fallen Explorers: Project Details

1. Our project is an inforgraphic designed to engage younger and casual audiences.

2. It is designed to foster sientific temperament and curiosity about space through interesting and simple stories.

3. We have used multiplicity of tools including but not limited to: Claude AI, Gemini, Adobe Photoshop, Ibix Paint, Blender 3.0, Writer Journal, the official detailing from NASA and ESA, Wikipedia, YouTube Videos for research, and old infographics from our childhood.

4. It anthromorphises the abandoned machinery and gives out a blend of melancholy and hope. It forces the reader to engage with the story emotionally, and in the end look at the Scientific Facts in a new light. It is complemented with chimercal and semi-to-scale imagery with different elements such as colourful rings of Saturn, which while being unreal and chimerical, still instill child-like wonder.

5. The factors considered are corollary to what is mentioned in the previous four points. The key guiding light in not just the science, but curiosity and natural wonder, and the end result of viewing Scientific Information in a new light.
